body: We should expand this to include all svg images that are drawn into `<canvas>` (rather than limiting this to `<foreignObject>`), possibly by updating the [svg spec](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/single-page.html#conform-processing-modes) to reference this. There are currently interop differences around drawing svg images into `<canvas>` (https://jsfiddle.net/qhkyob4z/4/) which this will resolve. We have data from Chrome that indicates [0.55% of page views](https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/1835) draw svg into canvas.

cc @whatwg/canvas

Some of these are already handled by the fact that when an `<svg>` image is drawn through `drawImage()` its document is in the [animated-image-document mode](https://svgwg.org/specs/integration/#animated-image-document-mode), which thus runs in the [secure-animated-mode](https://svgwg.org/specs/integration/#secure-animated-mode) which does forbid script execution, interactivity and external references. (`drawImage()` also adds the limitation that animated images should draw their first frame).  
This means that cross-origin resources (external references) should not load, and selection, find in page, spell-check, auto-fill should not run.  

This leaves non-default colors, fonts(?), themes, and preferences (including rendering of scrollbars), subpixel text rendering and antialiasing, platform-specific appearance of form associated elements, and visited link information. For that latter I wonder if asking to treat the SVG document as an opaque origin wouldn't solve that, since they can't have external references anyway.

@progers regarding your fiddle, I should note that the `AccentColor` interop also affects `fillStyle = "AccentColor"`, which is supported in Firefox and Safari but not in Chrome, even though it's already accessible through `getComputedStyle()` or even `color-mix`. https://jsfiddle.net/0eysu9ko/
